The contrast does not reflect an inhibition paradigm (no Go/No-Go, Stroop, or similar); it isolates working memory/vigilance demands rather than inhibitory control.
This is not a task-switching or set-shifting paradigm; the contrast does not index switching demands.
The task is not a planning paradigm (no Tower-type planning manipulation); it does not index planning demands.

During VT participants continuously monitor repeated verbal sequences and signal detected transformations (target detection), requiring sustained attention/set maintenance—consistent with vigilance demands; the VT>baseline contrast reflects this increased monitoring demand.
This is not a word generation/verbal fluency initiation task; the contrast does not index self-initiated generation.

Initiation annotations require word-generation/verbal-fluency paradigms (self-initiated generation). This analysis is a cued picture-naming semantic interference contrast, not a generation > repetition contrast, so it does not meet INITIATION_I1/I2.

The SUPPRESS > FREE-THOUGHT contrast is a within-group, whole-brain task activation contrast reflecting the executive demand to suppress (inhibit) thoughts versus free thought. This fits the pooled executive-function category (task maps to an executive domain and the contrast reflects executive demand).
The task is not a working-memory paradigm (no n-back, Sternberg, delay, or load manipulation); the contrast isolates thought-suppression rather than working memory.

Although conceptually suppressing a thought involves inhibitory control, the local inclusion criteria require standard inhibition paradigms (Go/No-Go, Stroop, Flanker, antisaccade), which this task does not employ; thus it does not meet the specified inhibition-task criteria.
The contrast does not involve task-switching or set-shifting; it does not meet the flexibility paradigm criteria.
This is not a planning paradigm (no Tower tasks or planning-move contrasts); it isolates a different domain.
The task is not a vigilance/oddball paradigm requiring sustained target detection; it isolates thought-suppression rather than set maintenance.
This is not a word-generation/initiation paradigm; the contrast does not reflect self-initiated generation.

The CLEAR > FREE-THOUGHT contrast is a within-group, whole-brain task activation contrast reflecting the executive demand to clear the mind of all thoughts versus free thought; this constitutes an executive control demand and meets pooled criteria.
The task is not a working-memory paradigm (no load/manipulation or delay); the contrast isolates thought-clearing rather than working memory.
Although clearing thoughts requires control, it does not match the specified inhibition paradigms (Go/No-Go, Stroop, etc.), so it fails the local inclusion criteria for inhibition.
The contrast does not involve switching between tasks or rules; it does not meet flexibility criteria.
This is not a planning paradigm (no Tower tasks or planning contrasts); it isolates a different domain.
CLEAR is not an oddball or target-detection sustained-attention task; it does not meet vigilance criteria.
The contrast does not involve verbal or behavioral generation/initiation tasks (e.g., word generation); it does not meet initiation criteria.

The CLEAR > SUPPRESS contrast compares two executive-control conditions (clearing all thoughts vs suppressing a particular thought); it is a within-group, whole-brain contrast that reflects executive demand and fits the pooled executive-function category.
This contrast does not reflect a working-memory paradigm or load/maintenance manipulation; it isolates different executive processes.

Though both conditions involve control over thought, the local inclusion criteria for inhibition require canonical motor/response-inhibition paradigms (e.g., Go/No-Go, Stroop), which are not used here.
This contrast does not involve task-switching or set-shifting per the flexibility criteria.
Not a planning task (no Tower or multi-move planning contrast); it isolates thought-control processes instead.
Not an oddball or sustained-attention target-detection contrast; does not meet vigilance criteria.
Not an initiation/word-generation paradigm; the contrast reflects thought-control rather than initiation.

The contrast does not reflect a working-memory paradigm or memory-load manipulation; it isolates thought-suppression vs free thinking.
Despite involving suppression, the task is not one of the canonical inhibition paradigms required by the local inclusion criteria, so it does not meet the inhibition annotation.
The contrast does not involve task switching or set-shifting; it fails the flexibility inclusion criteria.
This is not a planning paradigm; it isolates thought-control rather than planning processes.
